jp_verse: 縁側に　赤茶の犬が座り\n\n    伸ばした舌だけが　笑みを伝えていた
en_verse: Upon the engawa a reddish-brown dog sat still,\nwhile only its outstretched tongue carried the smile.

jp_verse: 木の升に　白米が満ち溢れ\n\n    朝の光だけが　稲の輝きを映した
en_verse: The wooden measure brimmed with white rice,\nwhile only the morning light mirrored the grain's glow.

jp_verse: 夕空に　灯籠が次々と浮かび\n\n    坂の町だけが　橙の光に包まれた
en_verse: Into the evening sky the lanterns rose one by one,\nwhile only the hillside town wrapped itself in orange light.

jp_verse: 満月の下　石畳の道が続き\n\n    障子の灯りだけが　夜を温めていた
en_verse: Beneath the full moon the stone path wound on,\nwhile only the light through shoji warmed the night.

jp_verse: 指先で　小さな楔を打ち込み\n\n    「匠」の文字だけが　静かに見守っていた
en_verse: At his fingertips he drove a tiny peg,\nwhile only the character for master craftsman watched in silence.

jp_verse: 縁側にもたれ　頬杖をつき\n\n    庭の灯籠だけが　午後を映していた
en_verse: Leaning on the engawa she rested on her elbow,\nwhile only the garden lantern mirrored the afternoon.

jp_verse: 工房の床に　削り屑が積もり\n\n    老いた職人だけが　技を研いでいた
en_verse: Wood shavings gathered upon the workshop floor,\nwhile only the aged craftsman honed his skill.

jp_verse: 本棚に囲まれ　老人が筆を執り\n\n    差し込む光だけが　知を照らしていた
en_verse: Surrounded by shelves the old man held his brush,\nwhile only the light streaming in illuminated his knowledge.

jp_verse: 石の上に　卜の枝が立ち\n\n    夕陽だけが　山を静かに照らした
en_verse: Upon the stones a divining rod stood tall,\nwhile only the setting sun quietly lit the mountains.

jp_verse: 神社の枝に　おみくじが結ばれ\n\n    夕光だけが　運命を漂わせた
en_verse: Upon the shrine branch omikuji slips were tied,\nwhile only the evening light drifted over fate.

jp_verse: 青空に　幟の凧が舞い\n\n    長い糸だけが　地面とつないでいた
en_verse: Against the blue sky a banner kite danced,\nwhile only its long string connected to the earth.

jp_verse: 石段の下　猫が丸くなり\n\n    朝日だけが　参道を照らしていた
en_verse: Beneath the stone step the cat curled round,\nwhile only the morning sun lit the shrine path.

jp_verse: 床の間に　梅と椿が置かれ\n\n    余白の静けさだけが　卓を研いでいた
en_verse: Within the tokonoma plum and camellia were placed,\nwhile only the stillness of open space refined the alcove.

jp_verse: 茅葺の里に　朝日が差し込み\n\n    谷の霧だけが　黄金に染まっていた
en_verse: Into the thatched village the morning sun streamed,\nwhile only the valley mist turned to gold.

jp_verse: 門の隙間に　三人の子が覗き\n\n    押さえた口だけが　笑いを隠していた
en_verse: Through the gate's narrow gap three children peered,\nwhile only their covered mouths hid the laughter.

jp_verse: 点てる前に　一本の指が立ち\n\n    静かな気配だけが　室を包んでいた
en_verse: Before whisking tea a single finger rose,\nwhile only the quiet presence filled the room.

jp_verse: 岩場で　少女が貝を掌に\n\n    波の記憶だけが　微笑みに残っていた
en_verse: Upon the rocky shore the girl cradled a shell,\nwhile only the sea's memory lingered in her smile.

jp_verse: 畳の部屋で　ヘアブラシをマイクに\n\n    幼い声だけが　夕を明るくした
en_verse: In the tatami room she sang into a hairbrush,\nwhile only a child's voice brightened the evening.

jp_verse: 雪の参道に　武士が立ち\n\n    揺るぎぬ姿だけが　灯籠に映った
en_verse: Upon the snowy shrine path the samurai stood,\nwhile only his unwavering form reflected in the lanterns.

jp_verse: 紺の作務衣に　四人が並び\n\n    縁側の光だけが　職を温めていた
en_verse: In indigo samue four stood side by side,\nwhile only the light from the engawa warmed their work.
